body.statement:
Assume \(d_e(G)<\infty\), a valid source-prime chart package \(\mathfrak C_{G,e}\) is supplied, and fix a successful finite output of \(\mathrm{thm:conditional\mbox{-}geometric\mbox{-}resolution}\). There are events \(\mathcal H_m\) with \(\inf_{\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G}\Pr_{\Sigma}(\mathcal H_m)\to1\) such that, on \(\mathcal H_m\), \(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m}\) is nonempty and is bijectively matched to \(\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma)\). With the empty-set convention in \(d_H\), uniformly over \(\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G\), \(d_H(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m},\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma))=O_{\mathbb P}(m^{-1/2})\) and \(\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G}\Pr_{\Sigma}(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m}=\varnothing)\to0\). Under local branch labels,
\[
\sqrt m\{r(\pi_G(S_m))-r(\Sigma)\}\rightsquigarrow N\!\left(0,Dr(\Sigma)D\pi_G(\Sigma)V_\Sigma D\pi_G(\Sigma)^{\mathsf T}Dr(\Sigma)^{\mathsf T}\right).
\]
The simultaneous neighborhoods \(\mathcal A_m\) cover every retained branch with asymptotic probability at least \(1-\alpha\), uniformly on \(\mathcal K_G\).
body.proof_tex:
Let \(q=n(n+1)/2\), fix an ordering \(\operatorname{vech}\) of symmetric entries, and define
\[
 W_r=\operatorname{vech}\!\left(X^{(r)}X^{(r)\mathsf T}-\Sigma\right).
\tag{27}
\]
Then
\[
 \sqrt m\,\operatorname{vech}(S_m-\Sigma)
 =m^{-1/2}\sum_{r=1}^m W_r.
\tag{28}
\]
Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid\mbox{-}gaussian}\), the summands are independent and centered.  Differentiating the Gaussian moment-generating function gives
\[
 \mathbb E_\Sigma(X_iX_jX_kX_l)
 =\sigma_{ij}\sigma_{kl}+\sigma_{ik}\sigma_{jl}+\sigma_{il}\sigma_{jk},
\tag{29}
\]
so
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_\Sigma(W_{r,ij},W_{r,kl})
 =\sigma_{ik}\sigma_{jl}+\sigma_{il}\sigma_{jk}
 =(V_\Sigma)_{ij,kl}.
\tag{30}
\]
Compactness of \(\mathcal K_G\) uniformly bounds every fixed Gaussian moment, including \(\mathbb E_\Sigma\|W_r\|^3\).  For each fixed \(u\in\mathbb R^q\), Taylor expansion of the characteristic function, with its remainder controlled by this third moment, gives uniformly in \(\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G\)
\[
 \mathbb E_\Sigma\exp\!\left(\frac{i u^{\mathsf T}W_r}{\sqrt m}\right)
 =1-\frac{u^{\mathsf T}V_\Sigma u}{2m}+O(m^{-3/2}).
\tag{31}
\]
Taking the \(m\)-th power proves
\[
 \sqrt m\,\operatorname{vech}(S_m-\Sigma)
 \rightsquigarrow N(0,V_\Sigma)
\tag{32}
\]
uniformly on \(\mathcal K_G\).  Indeed, along every sequence in the compact class, a convergent covariance subsequence exists; (31) identifies its unique weak limit, while the uniformly bounded second moments give tightness.  Chebyshev's inequality also yields
\[
 \|S_m-\Sigma\|=O_{\mathbb P}(m^{-1/2})
\tag{33}
\]
uniformly.

On the projection tube write \(\widehat\Sigma_m=\pi_G(S_m)\).  The projection fixes its smooth stratum, so \(\pi_G(\Sigma)=\Sigma\).  Smoothness on a neighborhood of the compact set and Taylor's theorem give
\[
 \operatorname{vech}(\widehat\Sigma_m-\Sigma)
 =D\pi_G(\Sigma)\operatorname{vech}(S_m-\Sigma)
 +O_{\mathbb P}(\|S_m-\Sigma\|^2)
\tag{34}
\]
uniformly.  Every coefficient circuit of \(p_e\) is smooth near \(\mathcal K_G\), because its denominator has a positive minimum there.  The preceding root-separation lemma supplies a common separation margin and a positive lower bound for \(|\partial_t p_e|\).  The implicit-function argument applied to
\(p_e(\Sigma,r_j(\Sigma))=0\) therefore gives one unique smooth branch through each retained root, with uniformly bounded first and second derivatives on a finite cover, and
\[
 Dr_j(\Sigma)[H]
 =-\frac{D_\Sigma p_e(\Sigma,r_j(\Sigma))[H]}
         {\partial_t p_e(\Sigma,r_j(\Sigma))}.
\tag{35}
\]
Increasing order, uniform separation, and the constant extension labels built into \(\mathrm{def:regular\mbox{-}cell}\) give the common labeling \(r=(r_1,\ldots,r_J)\).  Equations (32)--(35), Taylor's theorem, and multiplication of characteristic functions by remainders converging to zero in probability yield
\[
 \sqrt m\{r(\pi_G(S_m))-r(\Sigma)\}
 \rightsquigarrow N\!\left(0,
 Dr(\Sigma)D\pi_G(\Sigma)V_\Sigma
 D\pi_G(\Sigma)^{\mathsf T}Dr(\Sigma)^{\mathsf T}
 \right)
\tag{36}
\]
uniformly on \(\mathcal K_G\).

All certificate factors are continuous and nonzero on \(\mathcal K_G\), and extension labels are locally constant on the selected cell.  Compactness supplies a relative neighborhood \(U\) on which the projection is defined, all certificate factors remain valid, and precisely the same \(J\) branches are retained.  With \(\gamma\) from the separation lemma, define
\[
 \mathcal H_m=\left\{
 \begin{array}{l}
 S_m\text{ lies in the projection tube},\quad \widehat\Sigma_m\in U,\\[2pt]
 \displaystyle\max_{1\leq j\leq J}
 |r_j(\widehat\Sigma_m)-r_j(\Sigma)|<\gamma/3
 \end{array}
 \right\}.
\tag{37}
\]
Uniform consistency in (33)--(34), uniform continuity of the finitely many root maps, and the positive certificate margins imply
\[
 \inf_{\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G}\Pr_\Sigma(\mathcal H_m)\longrightarrow1.
\tag{38}
\]
On \(\mathcal H_m\), \(\mathrm{thm:real\mbox{-}root\mbox{-}lifting}\) and \(\mathrm{def:finite\mbox{-}set\mbox{-}estimator}\) give
\[
 \widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m}
 =\{r_1(\widehat\Sigma_m),\ldots,r_J(\widehat\Sigma_m)\}.
\tag{39}
\]
The margin in (37) makes (39) a bijective matching to \(\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma)\).  By \(\mathrm{lem:regular\mbox{-}cell\mbox{-}existence}\), \(J\geq1\), so the estimated set is nonempty on \(\mathcal H_m\).  Moreover,
\[
 d_H(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m},\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma))
 \leq\max_j|r_j(\widehat\Sigma_m)-r_j(\Sigma)|
 =O_{\mathbb P}(m^{-1/2})
\tag{40}
\]
uniformly.  Formally, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), first use (38) to make \(\Pr_\Sigma(\mathcal H_m^c)<\varepsilon/2\) uniformly, and then choose the constant in the \(O_{\mathbb P}\) bound on the right side of (40) to make its exceedance probability below \(\varepsilon/2\).  This also handles the stipulated infinite Hausdorff distance on \(\mathcal H_m^c\).  Finally,
\[
 \sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G}
 \Pr_\Sigma(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m}=\varnothing)
 \leq\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G}\Pr_\Sigma(\mathcal H_m^c)
 \longrightarrow0.
\tag{41}
\]

It remains to construct simultaneous neighborhoods.  Let \(s=\dim\mathcal C_{G,e}\) and
\[
 W_\pi(\Sigma)=D\pi_G(\Sigma)V_\Sigma D\pi_G(\Sigma)^{\mathsf T}.
\tag{42}
\]
For any nonzero symmetric direction \(H\), (29) gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_\Sigma(X^{\mathsf T}HX)
 =2\operatorname{tr}\!\left((\Sigma^{1/2}H\Sigma^{1/2})^2\right)>0,
\tag{43}
\]
because \(\Sigma\succ0\).  Hence \(V_\Sigma\) is positive definite on symmetric-coordinate directions.  The nearest-point projection fixes the stratum; its derivative is the identity on the tangent space and has that \(s\)-dimensional space as image.  Therefore \(W_\pi\) has constant rank \(s\).  Compactness bounds its smallest positive eigenvalue away from zero, so its Moore--Penrose inverse is continuous.  With the continuous plug-in matrix \(\widehat W_{\pi,m}\), (32)--(34) and continuous mapping yield
\[
 m\,\operatorname{vech}(\widehat\Sigma_m-\Sigma)^{\mathsf T}
 \widehat W_{\pi,m}^{+}
 \operatorname{vech}(\widehat\Sigma_m-\Sigma)
 \rightsquigarrow\chi_s^2
\tag{44}
\]
uniformly.  To see the limiting law directly, diagonalize \(W_\pi\): for \(Z\sim N(0,W_\pi)\), the quadratic form \(Z^{\mathsf T}W_\pi^+Z\) is the sum of \(s\) independent squared standard normal variables.

Let \(E_m\) be the corresponding confidence ellipsoid centered at \(\widehat\Sigma_m\), intersected with the regular projected neighborhood, and use the \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of \(\chi_s^2\).  Equation (44) gives
\[
 \liminf_{m\to\infty}\inf_{\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G}
 \Pr_\Sigma(\Sigma\in E_m)\geq1-\alpha.
\tag{45}
\]
If \(s=0\), use the degenerate ellipsoid at the locally constant projected point, whose limiting coverage is one.  Define \(\mathcal A_{m,j}=r_j(E_m)\), as in \(\mathrm{def:branch\mbox{-}neighborhoods}\).  Whenever \(\Sigma\in E_m\), every inclusion \(r_j(\Sigma)\in\mathcal A_{m,j}\) holds simultaneously.  Thus
\[
 \liminf_{m\to\infty}\inf_{\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G}
 \Pr_\Sigma\!\left(
 r_j(\Sigma)\in\mathcal A_{m,j}\text{ for all }1\leq j\leq J
 \right)\geq1-\alpha,
\tag{46}
\]
which covers every retained branch and selects none.
body.justification: The observationally equivalent branches are the estimand, so inference must cover them simultaneously rather than select one.
body.gap: Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer treat general criterion-defined sets, while Mareis, Sturma, and Drton derive regular half-trek point inference; neither gives root-specific joint inference for a finite algebraic SEM coordinate fiber.
body.consumer: Researchers using a graph with added parents can report sampling uncertainty around every compatible direct-effect branch.
